basis: Fresh independent actual-scope/defined-term adjudication. Original independent report and pre-adjudication results retained.

changes.reason: The answer expressly says "Cover four R building slots with ruins" and then hides the specified items "one under each ruin, shuffling stacks to conceal identities". Taken together these specify the required map locations and randomization. The answer never instructs the player to leave the ruins off the map or gives a competing final location. A separate "return each stack" sentence would be clearer, but repeating the already specified final R-slot destination is not an additional unresolved substantive fact in this wording. This is not credit borrowed from another question. All other requested setup particulars are present. The broad setup policy requires the material arrangement and shuffle, not a mandatory sequence of synonymous verbs.

Both answers explicitly allow repeated pawn activation with a hammer payment for each icon, reject the mixed-suit craft, and say the crafted item can "immediately be taken face up" into Satchel/track. Face up is the operative ready state, not merely a delayed acquisition. Under the ordinary item rule that is a substantive answer that the item is immediately available; no extra refresh or later-turn wait is imposed. Requiring the literal phrase "may immediately use it" would require redundant wording rather than a missing rule. This does not grant actions whose other prerequisites are absent or retroactive refresh benefits. It relies on the defined meaning of face up, not an answer at another ID.

"Exhaust any one item" uses a defined operation. Under Law 9.2.5 and the summary definition, exhausting an item already means selecting a face-up undamaged item and flipping it down. The quantifier any permits any item type; it does not override the verb's eligibility. Restating ready and undamaged would be clearer but adds no unresolved cost rule. This is the same reason that face-up readiness can substantively resolve immediate item availability at Q56: established technical meanings count. The same answer supplies the matching card, target including Hostile, optional item acquisition, non-Hostile limitation, same-turn count and one-improvement-per-Aid constraint. Failure to mention scoring the new relationship space is not a requested omission for the fixed counting question.
